subject: Confidence intervals for correlations between latent variables

messages.author: bdd9db9664b36074
messages.subject: Confidence intervals for correlations between latent variables
parts:
Hi all, 

In my model I have specified covariance paths between my latent factors e.g.

Mod1 ' <- 

SF7 ~~ AT7
SF10 ~~ AT10
SF13 ~~ AT13'

I am aware that lavaan automatically computes the correlation between all of my latent variables within my model and I have retrieved these using this command lavInspect(Mod1, "cor.lv"). This gives me:











Would anyone be able to advise me on how to get the confidence intervals for these correlation coefficients?

Best wishes,
Hannah

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals for correlations between latent variables
parts: Would anyone be able to advise me on how to get the confidence intervals for these correlation coefficients?

That output is just the standardized model-implied covariance matrix among common factors.  You can get SEs from the standardizedSolution() output, but I wouldn't construct normal-theory CIs from them because standardized parameters have boundaries that the CI might cross.  If you set the argument "std.lv = TRUE" to identify the latent scale by fixing factor variances to 1, then your estimated covariances are correlations, so you can use those confidence intervals from summary(fit, ci = TRUE) or parameterEstimates(fit).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals for correlations between latent variables
parts: So there is no function implemented to have that done automatically?

I doubt it.  People typically report CIs for their parameter estimates, not for their accompanying standardized measures of effect size.  The formulas are not difficult to look up and type out, but an even easier solution would be to standardize your variables and fit the same SEM to the standardized data, then look at those CIs.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

On Saturday, September 3, 2016 at 4:18:35 AM UTC-4, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
So there is no function implemented to have that done automatically?

I doubt it.  People typically report CIs for their parameter estimates, not for their accompanying standardized measures of effect size.  The formulas are not difficult to look up and type out, but an even easier solution would be to standardize your variables and fit the same SEM to the standardized data, then look at those CIs.

In fact, in typical applications of SEM, we are concerned about standardized coefficients as scales do not matter. That is why SEM software should provide an option that outputs CIs for standardized parameters.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals for correlations between latent variables
parts: In fact, in typical applications of SEM, we are concerned about standardized coefficients as scales do not matter. That is why SEM software should provide an option that outputs CIs for standardized parameters.

There is an option:

?bootstrapLavaan()

You can use the bootstrap CI as a measure of uncertainty about the estimate, or you can just use the SE from the standardizedSolution() output to measure uncertainty.  But if you want to use the CI as an inverted hypothesis test (to answer the question: With which parameters are my data consistent? or Which null hypotheses could I not reject), the typical null hypothesis of 0 applies just as easily to an unstandardized vs. standardized estimate.  So unless you are testing a different null hypothesis (e.g., that a correlation == 1), it seems arbitrary whether you use a p value or CI as well as whether you use the unstandardized or standardized solution.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
